question: Can large language models stand in for people in social measurement?

threads.name: Digital twins of respondents
threads.blurb: Can a large language model given a person's profile reproduce that person's survey answers? Where it succeeds, it is a measurement tool. Where it fails, the failure is the finding.

wip.title: Opinion change in twins
wip.desc: Do persona twins change their views the way the people they model do?

wip.title: What conditioning encodes
wip.desc: Which parts of a persona the model actually represents internally.

wip.title: Detecting synthetic respondents
wip.desc: Telling survey answers written by a model apart from human ones.

threads.name: Validity of social simulation
threads.blurb: The same question for a whole population: do agents built on large language models reproduce social processes, or only their outcomes? A simulation can match the outcome while the process behind it is wrong.

papers.title: Persona-Based Simulation of Human Opinion at Population Scale

threads.name: Who social media speaks for
threads.blurb: My dissertation. Inferring demographics and stance from social media posts, and asking whom that expression represents.

threads.name: Large language models as survey instruments
threads.blurb: AI interviewers, and coding of open-ended survey answers with large language models, built and evaluated as survey instruments.

wip.title: Evaluating AI interviewers
wip.desc: A testbed and metrics for survey interviews conducted by an AI interviewer.

wip.title: Coding open-ended answers
wip.desc: Coding open-ended answers with large language models, checked against human coders.

threads.name: Structuring text at scale
threads.blurb: Methods the other threads rely on: fast ranking and summarization of large collections of posts.
